chunks: My father, my brother, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan all narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Idris ibn Ahmad, from Abu 'Abdillah al-Jamurani, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Sandal [Safwan], from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:

I was sitting in the house of Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) and I looked at the cooing pigeon cooing for a long time. Then Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) looked at me and said, 'O Dawud! Do you know what this bird is saying?' I said, 'No, by Allah, may I be your ransom.' He said, 'It is calling down curses on the killers of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him). Therefore, keep it in your houses.' And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Abu 'Abdillah al-Jamurani, through his chain, similarly.

key_terms.الرَّاعِبِيِّ: A specific type of pigeon known for its cooing
key_terms.يُقَرْقِرُ: Cooing or making a low humming sound

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the pigeon's cooing in Shia tradition according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the Shia belief in the spiritual awareness of creation, where the specific 'ra'ibi' pigeon is understood to continuously invoke divine curses upon the killers of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.). The Imam’s instruction to keep these birds in homes serves both as a physical reminder of the Ahl al-Bayt’s suffering and a means of perpetuating the *du'a* of the natural world against their oppressors. This tradition underscores the interconnectedness of the material and spiritual realms in Shia cosmology, where even animals participate in the cosmic narrative of justice and vengeance.
